rationale.conceptual: The method is an established workflow (DFT + harmonic/anharmonic IFC + ShengBTE), but it involves non-trivial physics (phonon scattering, BTE) and careful parameter selection (supercell size, cutoff, q-grid). Requires understanding of the specific code outputs and branch-averaging.
rationale.execution: The pipeline has multiple stages: DFT optimization, harmonic force constants with phonopy (many finite displacements), anharmonic force constants with thirdorder.py (many DFT runs), ShengBTE iterative solution, and post-processing to extract branch-averaged quantities. Orchestrating these tools, managing supercell generation and calculations, and ensuring convergence make it a fragile multi-tool pipeline (~6 stages).

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires implementing a multi-step DFT-based lattice thermal conductivity workflow (VASP/QE, phonopy, thirdorder.py, ShengBTE) for two boron structures. The method is standard but involves understanding phonon scattering and BTE. The pipeline is moderately long with several handoffs. Resource needs are modest CPU-only DFT calculations on small supercells.

compute_estimate.reasoning: DFT calculations on supercells up to 256 atoms with plane-wave basis set; memory per calculation a few GB; all CPU-bound. Input data are tiny structure files. No large datasets needed.
